sonnet.problem: Card 6 already asked about Revelation 9:4 and showed that the locusts may not harm the grass, plants and trees. Card 7 asks about the same verse and its question repeats that fact ('If not the grass, plants and trees...'). It re-asks the same fact instead of asking something new.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The question says the riders' breastplates are 'the colors of fire, sapphire and sulfur'. The right answer is 'Fire and smoke and sulfur', so the question holds forms of its own answer and hints at which choice is right.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the last word of a line from the text ('in their mouths and in their ___'). No earlier card sets up tails on the horses, so the baker can only guess the wording.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
